newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oil close firm, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oil close firm, but off highs.

text.p: Closing European vegetable oil prices were firm, supported by further gains in Chicago, but off there highs for the day at the close on Monday.
"Chicago didn't open as high as some people thought it would and prices came of slightly towards the close as a result," said a trader.
Concern over weather in Brazil and a bullish USDA report on Friday continued to support the U.S. market.
Earlier a higher to limit up close in Chicago on Friday had pushed palm oil prices higher in Asia triggering gains on the Europe market.
Trade, however, was slow in Europe with no business reported in crude palm oil or the lauric oil markets.
Refined palm oil saw some active trading in the Far East, but nothing feed through to Europe.
In Soft oils most of the business was switching between soy oil and rape oil, but traders said it was mainly three way switching and therefore was a true reflection of the market.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $5 up to unchanged while products were $2.50 to $12.50 higher.
Coconut oil finished $5 up and palmkernel oil $7.50 higher.
Dutch soy oil closed 1.50 to two guilders up after Feb/Apr traded at 96.50, May/Jul at 97.50, 97.75, 98.50 and 99 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Rapeoil finished 2.50 to 1.50 guilders up after Feb/Mar traded at 99 and 99.25 and Apr/Jun at 100.00 and 100.25 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
At the close the premium for rape oil over soy oil, based on sellers' prices was two to three guilders against two to 2.50 guilders at Friday's close.
